prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production RGBA sprite atlas for a layered paper pop-up Pokémon Emerald Seafloor Cavern battle terrarium. Generate a NEW 1536x1024 transparent atlas, exactly four columns and three rows of distinct isolated assets, each in its own equal cell with at least 20px fully transparent gutter. No labels, no grid, no background, no ground shadows outside the cutout. This is a collection of separate flat theatre set cards, not a whole cave scene.
Style: richly detailed hand-cut matte cardstock illustration. Each shape is recognizably a thin paper silhouette with visible cream cut edges, overlapping cut paper chips, hand-printed contour marks and fine paper fibres. Depth from stacked flat silhouettes and narrow contact shadows, never thick polygonal blocks or realistic sculpted rocks. Sophisticated blue-grey limestone and slate, warm salt/beige highlights, teal paper water, small muted moss and marine growth. Front-facing cards viewed slightly from above, coherent soft upper-left light.
Row 1 left to right: (1) jagged distant dark navy cave rock silhouette, many overlapping narrow paper strata, irregular skyline, no rectangular background; (2) asymmetrical tall left cave wall silhouette with thin horizontal strata and a small open natural arch cut THROUGH with transparency; (3) different tall right cave wall with small shelf notches and a few hanging olive paper seaweed leaves; (4) hanging stalactite fringe, five sharp separately layered paper teeth, flat top attachment strip, ivory cut edges.
Row 2: (1) medium stepped slate ledge front cutout with several thin laminated strata, salt patches and tiny barnacles, dry flat top; (2) broad irregular boulder grouping made from overlapping flat folded grey cards, three distinct boulders, no water or background; (3) wide low turquoise water strip made of layered blue paper ribbons and small white paper foam crescents, very clearly water, no rocks; (4) wide curling small wave strip with thin ivory paper foam scallops, teal/turquoise underside, light and elegant rather than giant storm wave.
Row 3: (1) low wide dry stone pedestal with flat beige top and layered blue slate fascia, sparse barnacle detail on sides, no water; (2) delicate branching olive/teal seaweed and modest ochre coral cluster made of individually overlapping thin paper fronds, no big rock; (3) small low group of pebbles, two pale shells and layered salt chips, natural uneven silhouette; (4) three separated pale-blue paper water droplets, varying sizes, vertically spaced so each can be cropped as an individual animated cutout.
Keep every subject entirely within its own cell. No realistic model lighting, no smooth extruded chunky 3D surfaces, no glowing effects. Preserve rich miniature craft detail without merging the elements into one backdrop.
